samples.summary: Canonical frontend design doc's `api/documents.ts` endpoint table not updated for the new copy API
samples.evidence: docs/design/frontend.md:425-434 keeps an authoritative table of every function in `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts` (including bulk `moveDocuments`/`deleteDocuments`). This change adds `copyDocument(id)` and `copyDocuments(ids)` plus `BulkCopyError` but does not add the rows, so the canonical subsystem doc is now stale. The new top-level `document-copy.md` mentions the functions in prose, but the repo's convention is to keep the subsystem inventory current rather than rely on a parallel feature doc.

samples.summary: New `POST /documents/:id/copy` endpoint missing from the backend endpoint tables (README + docs/design/backend.md)
samples.evidence: packages/backend/README.md:194-200 and docs/design/backend.md:163-187 enumerate the `/documents` routes with their auth tiers. The change adds a route with a deliberately *different* gate (workspace member, not manager) — exactly the kind of divergence those tables exist to record — but neither is updated.

samples.summary: `snapshotJsonRoot`/`asJsonRoot` re-implement the existing snapshot normalizer in `scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts` instead of sharing it, and drop its stronger fallbacks
samples.evidence: packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:81-108 already implements `parseJsonSnapshot` + `normalizeSnapshot` (identical string-unwrapping loop and identical 'Yorkie document root snapshot is not an object' error text), plus two extra fallbacks the new code omits: `escapeControlCharsInJson` and `detachYorkieValue` (lines 18-79, 110-144). The service duplicates the first two layers verbatim and stops there, so the very control-character documents the script needed layer 3 for can still fail a copy. This change already created a shared home for exactly this kind of helper (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts`) but did not put the snapshot logic there.

samples.summary: Extracting `unwrapJson` into a new shared module is scope creep — the copy feature never uses it and it still has exactly one consumer
samples.evidence: grep for `unwrapJson`/`yorkie-json` shows the only importer is `packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:27`; `document-copy.service.ts` does not import it (it hand-rolls `asJsonRoot` instead). The move therefore adds a file and an indirection without serving the change under review.

samples.summary: Design doc omits two non-obvious content-fidelity behaviours the implementation relies on: bigint/Long re-coercion and the `toJSON` parse fallback
samples.evidence: The doc details `stripComments` at length (lines 30-40, 95) but never mentions `reviveLongs` (document-copy.service.ts:236-258 — silently truncating every epoch-ms timestamp without it) nor the `JSON.stringify(getRoot())` fallback for control-character roots (document-copy.service.ts:284-291). Both are exactly the kind of arm a reader of the canonical doc would need to know about before adding a new JSON root type.

samples.summary: Goal "the copy is independent: deleting the source leaves it intact" is not qualified for embedded image blobs, which the copy shares with the source
samples.evidence: Sheet/board/docs content embeds images as workspace-scoped blob URLs (`SheetImage.src` → `/api/v1/workspaces/:wid/images/:id`, docs/design/sheets/sheet-image.md:41-52, 94-100) with no DB record. The whole-root JSON snapshot copies those `src` strings verbatim, so source and copy point at the same objects — unlike the `FileService.copy` path, which the doc explicitly justifies for independence. Today nothing deletes image blobs so the practical impact is nil, but the stated goal and the risks table say nothing about the asymmetry.

samples.summary: `target-version: 0.2.0` in the new design doc looks stale for a feature landing now
samples.evidence: Recent docs use current versions (docs/design/notifications.md:3 `0.7.0`, docs/design/design-editor/design-editor-local-plugin.md:3 `0.7.0`, board docs `0.6.3`); `0.2.0` is the value on the oldest docs (backend.md/frontend.md era).

samples.summary: Naming table does not describe the util's gap-reuse behaviour, and the `(copy N)` scheme diverges from the repo's existing unique-name convention
samples.evidence: `copyTitle` reuses holes in the numbering (`document-copy-title.util.spec.ts:25-29`: `Report`, `Report (copy)`, `Report (copy 3)` → `Report (copy 2)`), which the doc's monotonic table (lines 71-78) does not convey. Separately, the repo's existing collision helper `getUniqueTabName` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/tab-name.ts:74, reused by the backend at yorkie/tab-ops.ts:40) uses a bare `" (2)"` suffix; a second, differently-shaped convention is a taste call worth noting only.

finding.summary: Whole-root JSON snapshot for `sheet` copies comment threads, contradicting the design doc's Non-Goal "Comments … deliberately not carried over"
finding.evidence: Spreadsheet comment threads live *inside* the Yorkie root: `packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:94` declares `comments?: { … }` per worksheet and seeds `comments: {}` at creation (line 147); `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1318,1366` reads `ws.comments`. `copyContent` for `JSON_ROOT_TYPES = ['sheet','slides','board']` assigns *every* root key onto the target, so a copied sheet inherits the source's comment threads (bodies, authors, mentions) — exactly what docs/design/document-copy.md's Non-Goals section and the service's own class doc say is not carried over. Note the inconsistency across types: the `doc` arm goes through `readDocsRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:427), which does NOT read `root.comments` (declared in packages/frontend/src/types/docs-document.ts:24), so docs copies drop comments while sheet copies keep them. Either the doc's Non-Goal or the sheet arm is wrong.
